Triaged this issue with maintainers, here is the summary -
- When OpenBLAS 0.3.30 runs kernels with Apple M4 SME instructions, it breaks NumPy.
https://github.com/numpy/numpy/issues/29393
Minimal Working Reproducer can be found on the above issue.

- In Numba's case, this shows up in the `gufunc` tests, where NumPy returns a basically uninitialized array of random data (that we compare to Numba's correct answer as seen above).

- This appeared to be correlated with Python 3.14, but actually was because the only numpy package in Anaconda available for Python 3.14 was built with `openblas 0.3.30`.

- Confirmed this was an OpenBLAS problem by forcing `openblas 0.3.29` into previously failing Python 3.14 environment, and that fixed the NumPy behavior (as tested by Numba's test suite).
```
(numba_3.14) ~/Documents/dev/numba > conda remove libopenblas --force 
(numba_3.14) ~/Documents/dev/numba > conda install libopenblas==0.3.29 --force
```

```
(numba_3.14) ~/Documents/dev/numba > python -m numba.runtests numba.tests.npyufunc.test_gufunc.TestGUFunc.test_gufunc
.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 1 test in 0.163s

OK
```

* Hence, on conda package building - the best fix for this issue would be to either remove `openblas 0.3.30` from the build configuration and rebuild everything that depends on it or patch `openblas 0.3.30` to make the check for `SME` always fail and rebuild that one package.

Also,
* Can confirm this issue does not appear on older Apple CPUs (M1-M3)
* NumPy’s own wheels don’t suffer this issue because they link to Accelerate on macOS for BLAS rather than use OpenBLAS.

related:
https://github.com/OpenMathLib/OpenBLAS/issues/5414
https://github.com/OpenMathLib/OpenBLAS/pull/5423

body: @swap357 was there a resolution here or does this need to be re-opened?
